The A bank VVT solenoid circuit is shorted to ground. VVT is turned off on that bank.
The B bank intake cam is not reaching the timing the ECM asked for.
The B bank VVT solenoid circuit is shorted to ground. VVT is turned off on that bank.
The barometric sensor is inside the ECM on these cars. The ECM substitutes 1013 mbar.
The barometric sensor is inside the ECM. The ECM substitutes 1013 mbar.
The body network minus wire has failed.
The body network plus wire has failed.
The box drops to 1st and 2nd only. Readable only on PDU; generic readers show P1779.
The box goes to electronic limp home with an amber warning.
The box goes to mechanical limp home with an amber warning.
The box goes to mechanical limp home with an amber warning. Check for stability control codes first.
The box goes to mechanical limp home with an amber warning. Harsh shifts and this code on an XK8 have been cured by a new battery and TCM reflash, so check voltage first.
The box goes to mechanical limp home with an amber warning. Reconfigure with WDS or IDS.
The box stays in Normal mode. No warning.
The check is based on the sensors, so Jaguar lists sensor and wiring faults before the catalyst. Rule these out first.
The cluster has a CAN fault.
The conductor plate name comes from a Mercedes 722.6 repair guide. The Jaguar table says n2 and n3 sensor.
The crank and cam signals disagree. On AJ26 engines TSB 303-43 lists it for stalling. If tensioners have failed, check chain timing too.
The dampers default to firm and a fault message shows, so the car rides hard. PistonHeads reports wear in the wires to the dampers on CATS cars.
The dampers default to firm with a message.
The driver will not notice. The TCM uses rear wheel speed from the ABS module instead.
The DSC pump has failed. Warning light and message.
The ECM cannot drive the A bank (right side) cam timing solenoid properly, so that intake cam stops being advanced. Expect a flat feel low down, with the check engine light after two trips.
The ECM has not had the go-ahead from the security system, or lost its ignition feed for a moment.

The ECM has run out of fuel trim adding fuel on this bank. If P0171 is set too, it caps the engine at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars and reduces maximum revs on 4.2 cars and stops purge, which looks like restricted performance. A bank is the right side of the engine.

The ECM has run out of fuel trim adding fuel on this bank. If P0174 is set too, it caps the engine at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars and reduces maximum revs on 4.2 cars and stops purge, which looks like restricted performance. A bank is the right side of the engine.
The ECM has run out of fuel trim taking fuel away on this bank. If P0172 is set too, it caps the engine at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars and reduces maximum revs on 4.2 cars and stops purge.
The ECM has run out of fuel trim taking fuel away on this bank. If P0175 is set too, it caps the engine at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars and reduces maximum revs on 4.2 cars and stops purge.
The ECM has shut down control of the upstream sensor on that bank.
The ECM lost the ABS module on the network. Cruise stops and idle quality can suffer. Other modules often log CAN codes at the same time. Fix the first cause and clear them all.
The ECM lost the instrument pack. Engine speed and temperature data go missing at the cluster.
The ECM sees the starter request stuck on.
The ECM stops most of its self tests. The 2003 table calls this a keep-alive memory error.
The ECM supply is out of range. Check the battery and charging first, since low voltage causes many false faults on this car.
The ECM uses a default of 25 °C.
The ECM uses a default pressure figure.
The ECM uses coolant temperature instead.
The engine is capped at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars with reduced maximum revs on 4.2 cars with an amber warning.
The engine took too long to warm up for closed loop fuelling. The engine is capped at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars with reduced maximum revs on 4.2 cars.
The fuel pump module is not hearing the ECM on 4.2 cars.
The gearbox holds 4th (mechanical limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power.
The gearbox holds 4th (mechanical limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. After this code the box stays in limp until repaired and the code cleared.
The gearbox holds 4th (mechanical limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. Check the battery and alternator first.

The gearbox holds 4th (mechanical limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. Shows that P0721 is also present and ABS data is missing, so look at the ABS module as well.

The gearbox holds 4th (mechanical limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. This is the classic selector fault. A dry or badly adjusted cable can set it, as can a dirty plug. The car may work again after a restart.
The gearbox holds 5th (electronic limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power.

The gearbox holds 5th (electronic limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. Often the code for a hard gearbox failure: one XK8 with this code at 113,000 miles had a failed B clutch hub, forward drum and converter damage.
The gearbox holds 5th (electronic limp) with an amber warning and GEARBOX FAULT message, and the ECM limits engine power. The clutches are slipping or a speed signal is wrong.
The heater in sensor 1/1 is drawing too little current, which points to an open circuit. The ECM drops closed loop fuelling and purge on that bank.
The heater in sensor 1/1 is drawing too much current, which points to a short. The ECM drops closed loop fuelling and purge on that bank.
The heater in sensor 2/1 is drawing too little current, which points to an open circuit. The ECM drops closed loop fuelling and purge on that bank.
The heater in sensor 2/1 is drawing too much current, which points to a short. The ECM drops closed loop fuelling and purge on that bank.
The instrument cluster and ECM failed their security handshake.
The instrument cluster is not receiving key status.
The instrument cluster received a wrong key status number from the body module. The cluster needs reconfiguring with WDS.
The lock-up clutch is not applying, so expect higher revs and more fuel used at cruise. Check engine light only.
The MAF reference ground is faulty. The engine is capped at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars with reduced maximum revs on 4.2 cars with an amber warning.
The main engine management relay circuit is faulty. Jaguar lists it for stalling on AJ26 engines.

The number means a different physical cylinder on 4.0 and 4.2 engines. On a 4.0 the codes run 1 to 4 down the right bank then 5 to 8 down the left. On a 4.2 odd numbers are on the right and even on the left.
The output from the pump module to the pump is out of range on 4.2 cars.
The P/N signal disagrees with road speed.

The pedal sensor tracks disagree. On 4.0 cars the sensor is driven by a cable from the pedal, so slack or wrong adjustment can cause this. Red warning. On AJ26 engines the throttle drops to its mechanical guard. On AJ27 engines the throttle motor is cut and the engine is held at about 1000 to 1250 rpm by cutting fuel. On 4.2 engines the motor is disabled and the throttle sits at a default opening. Cruise and idle control stop working.
The private network to the steering angle and yaw sensors has failed.
The private sensor network has a transmit fault.
The pump relay circuit is faulty. On SC cars this is pump 1, and the ECM runs pump 2 to keep the engine going.
The red warning comes on and the throttle falls back to its mechanical guard position. Cruise, idle control, traction and power limiting are off.
The returnless 4.2 system controls pump speed from a pressure sensor. The ECM uses a default of 3.80 bar.
The sensor behind the catalyst is not switching.
The sensor behind the catalyst reads high.
The sensor behind the catalyst reads low.
The sensor is reacting too slowly. Closed loop and adaptive fuelling stop on that bank. Jaguar lists a misfire first, so fix any misfire before buying a sensor.
The sensor reads as very cold, usually an open circuit. The engine is capped at 3000 rpm on 4.0 cars with reduced maximum revs on 4.2 cars with an amber warning on the first trip.
The sensor reads as very hot. Either the engine really is overheating or the circuit is shorted. Check the real temperature before driving on.
The signal is missing at one rear wheel.
The signal is present but unreliable.
The signal is wrong or missing with the car moving. Check the sensor gap and for debris on it.
The signal reads as very cold air. The ECM substitutes 50 °C.
The signal reads as very hot air. The ECM substitutes 50 °C.
The small fan that cools the ECM is not working. Jaguar calls it the cool box fan on 4.0 cars.
The stability module received bad setup data.

The tank could not reach test pressure. Jaguar says this is usually the only EVAP code seen on XK8s and has two causes: a real large leak, or no vacuum because the purge valve is stuck shut. Fit the cap properly, clear the code and retest before buying parts.
The TCM changes out of the problem gear and tries again, so you may feel a double shift.
The TCM substitutes high torque and speed values to protect the box, or goes to electronic limp.
The TCM uses coolant temperature instead, with an amber warning.
The TCM uses coolant temperature. You may see HIGH TEMP GEARBOX.
The TCM uses output speed for vehicle speed.
The TCM uses stability control speed instead. No warning.
The TCM uses substitute values and the converter clutch stays released.

The throttle is not where the ECM commanded. Do the throttle relearn first if the battery has just been off. On AJ26 cars the throttle falls to its mechanical guard; on later cars it goes into limp home.
The throttle motor drive circuit has failed. Red warning and limp home or mechanical guard mode, depending on engine.
The traction switch circuit is faulty.

The two throttle position tracks disagree. Red warning. On AJ26 engines the throttle drops to its mechanical guard. On AJ27 engines the throttle motor is cut and the engine is held at about 1000 to 1250 rpm by cutting fuel. On 4.2 engines the motor is disabled and the throttle sits at a default opening. Cruise and idle control stop working. On 1999-2001 AJ27 cars a common cause is the tin and gold terminal mismatch at the sensor plug.
The wide range sensor ahead of the catalyst reports lean at the ECM. Check for a plain lean mixture too.
The wide range sensor ahead of the catalyst reports rich at the ECM.
Throttle adaptions not relearned after battery disconnect
Throttle is limited to 30% and engine speed reduced.
Throttle is limited to about 30% and shifts become harsh, because torque reduction requests are lost.

Throttle motor relay or its feed faulty
Throttle movement is limited, speed is capped at 80 mph and cruise is off.

Throttle return spring failed, meaning a throttle assembly fault

Throttle sensor wiring open or high resistance

Throttle, pedal, coolant, air temperature or tank pressure sensor failed

Track 1 sense wire shorted to voltage (sensor pin 3)

Transponder module to body module wiring
TSB 303-04 revises the pinpoint test for this code on the 1997 XK8.

TSB 303-08 covers VIN 001001-011682, with a bench test: apply battery voltage to the solenoid and check the plunger moves. If a scanner shows this on a supercharged car, suspect the ECM or wiring, since the MY2003 guide and JTIS show no VVT hardware on it. Late XKRs are unconfirmed: the 2006 US brochure lists cam phasing.
TSB 303-46 ties P0442, P0455 and P0446 on 2000-01 XKs (VIN A00083-A13691) to the canister close valve.
TSB title covers P0780 to P0785 and P0829 on 2003-05 XKs.

With no signal the engine has about a 50% chance of starting, but runs on if lost while running.

XKR intercooler coolant pump relay. Throttle is limited to about 30% with an amber warning, so the car feels badly down on power.
XKR sensor after the intercooler reads very hot. Throttle is limited to 30%. Jaguar lists intercooler failure first.
XKR sensor after the intercooler. Throttle is limited to 30% with an amber warning.
